justifications.durability: the check fails when the mechanism it pins is removed and only then: my passthrough mutant reddens it at the second assertion with the fabricated id surviving, and the run's own negative-control.log shows the same assertion red under the mutation it declares; with the resolver restored the module passes 4 of 4, and the control arm inside the same case keeps a resolvable citation, so an entry naming nothing is dropped as unresolvable rather than every entry being dropped; the case seeds its own one-commit repository under tmp_path and reads no state outside it, so it answers about the code rather than about this machine; it pins a private helper rather than a caller path, so a regression reachable only through a promotion or a refusal composer would still be caught only as far as that helper reaches
justifications.evidence: both arms reproduce independently at the reviewed head; I re-ran the whole module the case was added to and read 4 passed, EXIT=0 in head-module.log, which is the receipt the run's own -q log could not carry; I derived the resolver's behaviour directly on the finding's own strings in resolver-probe.log, reading ['f4471999de4d3b20376947353a3a763189012fcc'] for the pair, [] for the fabricated citation alone, and the real id alone, so the drop is a resolution rather than a dropping of everything; I falsified the new check myself in mutant-probe.log by replacing the tree lookup with a passthrough through a pytest plugin loaded from /tmp, which reddens exactly the assertion the run's own negative-control.log reddens, at 1 failed and EXIT=1, and the run's log opens with the declared mutation verbatim as its contract requires; the residual is the artifacts line, whose 40-added-lines figure does not reproduce against the commit's 51 insertions, and the manifest's statement that the new case passes rests on a count rather than on a named result
justifications.fit: the added constant, helper and case are named by what they do — a citation that names no object, a seed repository, a case that pins the resolver — and the docstrings state the mechanism rather than the finding that motivated them; the naming checks over the 51 added lines and the one path return nothing, and ruff check --no-cache passes with ruff format --check reporting the file already formatted; the helper is one module-level function the case alone uses, so it introduces no abstraction beyond the seeding it performs, and it reuses the module's existing tmp_path idiom rather than a new fixture
justifications.goal_fidelity: the named defect still stands in the record it was recorded against: I read /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260930T155953437797-a-repair-hold-names-its-cause/manifest.md, whose commits: field still carries 3b945ad92310e71ffdbfe2d1e80b7a1b0dba2b0d, and git cat-file -e on that string in the repository exits 1 against a passing control on the same instrument where the true head 3b945ad92e124c855330705d97862f3570ee7d53 resolves to the docs(evidence) commit the run made; the delivered change adds no product behaviour, so no reader of that record is served differently by it; what the node did reach is the propagation half and the naming of the true revision, which it states in its landing line, and it records the unreachable half as a follow-on rather than claiming a repair it did not make; the shortfall is that the instance is uncorrected
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat at 67930d30 is one path and 51 insertions, and it is the first of the three granted write paths; the fragment and the figure directory are granted but unused, which the node's own landing contract requires because its done-when names no artifact; nothing outside the grant was written, and the reviewed worktree reads clean under git status --porcelain after my arms ran in it with bytecode writing disabled
